pr_comments: Why disregard `maxSockets` when `maxTotalSockets` is set? I think that would still be useful to have.

> Why disregard `maxSockets` when `maxTotalSockets` is set? I think that would still be useful to have.

If both are retained, is it feasible to have `maxTotalSockets` as the first priority?

> If both are retained, is it feasible to have `maxTotalSockets` as the first priority?

It would have to be, yes. An easy way to implement this would be to default `maxTotalSockets` to `Infinity` if the option was not explicitly set. Also we should probably still make sure that a supplied value is at least not negative, maybe `> 0` too.
/cc @BridgeAR @addaleax @ronag

> I believe this is subtly broken. Consider the case:
> 
> We have maxed out the number of sockets. We try to schedule to an origin that has not active requests. We put the request directly into that queue. However, since this origin doesn't have any active request it will never be triggered to resume.

Yes, that's why we made the change that when removing the sockets, we determine that if there is a origin without an active request, then we execute the first request for this origin to make the origin active.

I've made some changes and hope to get some feedback.

/cc @ronag @mcollina @addaleax

issue_context.title: httpAgent.absoluteMaxSockets
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for suggesting an idea to make Node.js better.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.
-->

We are trying to ensure the maximum number of active connections from NodeJS to backend systems is maintained.  `httpAgent.maxSockets` behaves at a "per origin" level which is also dynamic and not completely deterministic.  This makes it difficult to create logic and patterns as the number of connections grows.  Instead we propose `absoluteMaxSockets` (or some other clever name), that enforces a maximum number of active sockets regardless of the origin.  

Doing this now is possible in the user space, but requires a great deal of code and logic to bind to each and every socket connection event and do the counting and enforcement, etc.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Assuming `httpAgent.absoluteMaxSockets` is implemented, if the number of open sockets across all origins grows beyond this number, the http agent would first attempt to check and see if any sockets can be closed, and if so attempt to close those sockets prior to opening a new one.
Assuming one cannot be open, an exception would be thrown at the time a request is made since a new socket connection cannot be opened.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As mentioned, we could implement this in user space, but it's tricky and cumbersome.
comments: Can I suggest you open a pull request with your proposed changes? It might get rejected but feature requests with working code stand a better chance of getting accepted than those without.
@bnoordhuis I'm willing to try to work on that if the demand is reasonable.

review_comments: I'm not sure this will work? It bypass the per origin logic, e.g. what if this specific origin is already at maxSockets? Also does it remove it from the freelist?
There is indeed this problem, maybe we can add a check whether this `specific origin` is already at `maxSockets` ?
I think we need some tests that hit this issue, and fix it afterwards.
Okay, I'll add some tests to cover this issue tomorrow morning.
I added the check and test cases.
But `ObjectKeys` traverses all the origin, which I think should be slower than running once `for loop`.
What's the reason for this newly added block, it doesn't seem to have anything to do with `maxTotalSockets` ?
Because of different origin, pending requests cannot be resolved.

eg:

Set conditions:
```
maxTotalSockets: 3

'localhost:3500:': Make 3 requests
'localhost:3600:': Make 3 requests
```

Socket allocation for two origin：
```
'localhost:3500:': 3
'localhost:3600:': 0
```
In the above case, requests from `'localhost:3600:'`  will not be resolved.
This doesn't actually remove the request from the list... the same request might/will get executed twice

I don't think that's going to happen.

The free event will be emitted when the socket is successfully created: 
See https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/33617/files#diff-5f7fb0850412c6be189faeddea6c5359R450

The delete request was done in the free event:
See https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/33617/files#diff-5f7fb0850412c6be189faeddea6c5359R125-R132

Just a note here... this logic will not be FIFO across origins. There might be older requests in a different origin, but if the origin which releases the socket has pending requests that will be prioritized.

Not sure if that's a problem... just noting for reference... does this need to be documented?
This is indeed a place to pay attention to, I will first documented.
